proofUses.reason: Corrected extinction conditioning leaves spatial steps independent; generation zero is counted separately. Geometric sums give the second-moment length and the existing finite-range Green theorem gives critical spatial decay in d>=3.

An exponential tilt makes the killed Green kernel into a positive-drift walk. Strong Markov gives a uniform upper bound, and one multinomial term gives a polynomial lower bound for the tilted occupation.

A generation second moment gives the lower bound. A bounded inverse-square comparison function dominates the projected branching hitting recursion, giving the upper bound. This proves comparison and logarithmic exponent, not an exact radius amplitude.
The Poisson-kernel identity and a transverse Gaussian expansion refine the exact axis rate; the occupation identity retains the exceptional-root normalization.

Uniform derivative bounds for the massive symbol difference give an absolute spatial remainder. The Gaussian resolvent determines the profile; the occupation identity supplies the Abel limit and the branching interpretation.
